RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is not evidence of discrimination. Academic hiring committees are often small and reflect departmental availability or subfield alignment rather than bias. Furthermore, search committees frequently weigh factors beyond publication count and teaching tenure—such as interview performance, curriculum needs, and relevant industry experience.

Raising the panel's gender without documentary proof of disparate treatment or procedural violations will severely damage your professional reputation and eliminate future opportunities. Instead, follow up politely on your request for constructive feedback. If you suspect procedural non-compliance, you may consult a union representative or university ombudsman confidentially, focusing strictly on objective criteria and process rather than the committee's demographic makeup.
